title: DR reflection plan: product layer (8 relationship changes)
rationale: Relationship schemas in the product layer that the maintainer-note triage and the sorting-question reflection (cli/scripts/spec-enrich) want removed, renamed, reversed or retargeted. Each operation carries the claims and Clef's sorting answers as evidence and the plan's probability. Accepting an operation means DR applies it with apply-walk.ts; rejecting means the schema stays.

operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of product.userworkflow.aggregates.business.businessprocess to product.userworkflow.realizes.business.businessprocess. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.68; claims rel:product.userworkflow#2.

evidence.quote: The relationship product.userworkflow aggregates business.businessprocess looks inverted; a user journey more naturally supports or realizes part of a business process. Proposed: Replace aggregates with supports or realizes, with the workflow supporting or realizing the business process.

Sorting answers (rel:product.userworkflow#2): best source of 'aggregates business.businessprocess': product.userworkflow (0.58), none (0.16), product.capability (0.07); best destination of 'product.userworkflow aggregates': business.businessprocess (0.62), none (0.16), business.businessevent (0.10); best predicate: realizes (0.68), triggers (0.06), none (0.06). Outcome: alternative (predicate=realizes).

operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of product.persona.realizes.motivation.stakeholder to product.persona.references.motivation.stakeholder. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.52; claims rel:product.persona#2.

evidence.quote: The relationship 'product.persona realizes motivation.stakeholder' is questionable because a fictional archetype does not implement a stakeholder. Proposed: Replace 'realizes' with 'associated-with' or introduce a dedicated 'represents' predicate.

Sorting answers (rel:product.persona#2): best source of 'realizes motivation.stakeholder': none (0.37), product.persona (0.34), product.feature (0.09); best destination of 'product.persona realizes': motivation.stakeholder (0.47), none (0.33), motivation.goal (0.07); best predicate: references (0.51), none (0.18), realizes (0.14). Outcome: alternative (predicate=references).

operations.rationale: Remove product.workflowstep.uses.product.capability: product.workflowstep.uses.product.feature already exists and expresses it. Plan kind retarget, p 0.77; claims rel:product.workflowstep#1.

evidence.quote: The relationships product.workflowstep uses product.capability and product.workflowstep uses product.feature overlap, because features realise capabilities and the step-to-capability link can be derived via step-to-feature-to-capability. Proposed: Keep the workflowstep-uses-capability relationship only for steps whose feature is not yet defined, treating it otherwise as derived from the feature link.

Sorting answers (rel:product.workflowstep#1): best source of 'uses product.capability': product.workflowstep (0.60), product.feature (0.21), none (0.07); best destination of 'product.workflowstep uses': product.feature (0.77), product.capability (0.11), none (0.06); best predicate: uses (0.40), none (0.27), depends-on (0.14). Outcome: alternative (target=product.feature).

operations.rationale: Remove product.feature.realizes.business.businessservice: application.applicationservice.realizes.business.businessservice already exists and expresses it. Plan kind retarget, p 0.62; claims rel:product.feature#3.

evidence.quote: The cross-layer product.feature realizes business.businessservice relationship may be redundant because application services usually realize business services, so the link is already implied via capability. Proposed: Consider removing the feature realizes businessservice relationship or relying on the path via capability.

Sorting answers (rel:product.feature#3): best source of 'realizes business.businessservice': application.applicationservice (0.62), application.applicationcomponent (0.14), business.businessprocess (0.12); best destination of 'product.feature realizes': business.businessservice (0.44), product.capability (0.27), none (0.10); best predicate: none (0.34), realizes (0.31), uses (0.13). Outcome: alternative (source=application.applicationservice).

operations.rationale: Retarget of product.userworkflow.uses.product.capability to product.feature.uses.product.capability. Plan kind retarget, p 0.53; claims rel:product.userworkflow#3.

evidence.quote: The relationship product.userworkflow uses product.capability is largely derivable via workflow steps to features to capabilities, so it is partly redundant. Proposed: Consider removing the direct uses relationship to capability since it is derivable through steps and features.

Sorting answers (rel:product.userworkflow#3): best source of 'uses product.capability': product.feature (0.53), product.workflowstep (0.22), product.userworkflow (0.16); best destination of 'product.userworkflow uses': product.capability (0.41), product.feature (0.23), none (0.21); best predicate: none (0.34), uses (0.28), depends-on (0.14). Outcome: alternative (source=product.feature).

operations.rationale: Remove product.workflowstep.serves.product.persona: product.userworkflow.serves.product.persona already exists and expresses it. Plan kind retarget, p 0.47; claims rel:product.workflowstep#2.

evidence.quote: The relationship product.workflowstep serves product.persona uses a loose predicate, since the persona performs the step; 'performed-by' would read more naturally. Proposed: Replace 'serves' with a 'performed-by' predicate for the workflowstep-to-persona relationship.

Sorting answers (rel:product.workflowstep#2): best source of 'serves product.persona': product.userworkflow (0.47), product.feature (0.16), product.workflowstep (0.15); best destination of 'product.workflowstep serves': product.persona (0.60), product.userworkflow (0.19), none (0.14); best predicate: serves (0.55), none (0.21), references (0.08). Outcome: alternative (source=product.userworkflow).

operations.rationale: Change of product.persona.serves.business.businessrole to business.businessfunction.references.business.businessrole. Plan kind compound, p 0.24; claims rel:product.persona#1.

evidence.quote: The relationship 'product.persona serves business.businessrole' is semantically wrong because a persona does not provide service to a role; it describes the people who fill the role. Proposed: Replace the 'serves' predicate with 'associated-with' or 'references'.

Sorting answers (rel:product.persona#1): best source of 'serves business.businessrole': business.businessfunction (0.25), none (0.22), business.businessinterface (0.15); best destination of 'product.persona serves': business.businessrole (0.38), none (0.36), business.businessactor (0.13); best predicate: references (0.53), none (0.21), realizes (0.16). Outcome: alternative (source=business.businessfunction; predicate=references).

operations.rationale: Change of product.userworkflow.composes.product.feature to product.userworkflow.uses.product.workflowstep. Claims disagree on the replacement (product.userworkflow.uses.product.workflowstep | product.workflowstep.uses.product.workflowstep); the first is proposed, the others are in dr.replacement for a re-proposal if this one is rejected. Plan kind conflict, p 0.56; claims node:product.userworkflow#1, rel:product.userworkflow#1.

evidence.quote: The 'composes' relationship from product.userworkflow to product.feature is questionable because a workflow exercises features through its steps rather than owning them. Proposed: Replace 'composes' with 'uses' or route the connection through product.workflowstep.

The relationship product.userworkflow composes product.feature is semantically wrong because features exist independently of any workflow and are shared across journeys. Proposed: Replace composes with aggregates or uses for the userworkflow-to-feature relationship.

Sorting answers (node:product.userworkflow#1): best source of 'composes product.feature': none (0.23), product.userworkflow (0.22), product.milestone (0.20); best destination of 'product.userworkflow composes': product.workflowstep (0.84), none (0.09), product.userworkflow (0.05); best predicate: uses (0.56), none (0.16), depends-on (0.07). Outcome: alternative (target=product.workflowstep; predicate=uses).

Sorting answers (rel:product.userworkflow#1): best source of 'composes product.feature': product.workflowstep (0.28), none (0.24), product.userworkflow (0.19); best destination of 'product.userworkflow composes': product.workflowstep (0.76), product.feature (0.11), none (0.07); best predicate: uses (0.72), depends-on (0.07), references (0.07). Outcome: alternative (source=product.workflowstep; target=product.workflowstep; predicate=uses).
